articles.title: In a Hoard of 5,500 Viking Age Coins, Archaeologists in Norway Found One So Rare That They Already Consider It a 'National Treasure'

paras.en: In April, metal detectorists stumbled upon a massive cache of 1,000-year-old silver coins in eastern Norway. At the time, archaeologists were impressed by the sheer size of the find, known as the Mørstad hoard, which totals thousands of coins and counting. They hailed it as the largest Viking Age coin stash ever found in Norway.

Now, researchers are even more excited about the cache. While cataloging the hoard, they found an exceedingly rare silver coin minted during the reign of Olaf II Haraldsson, a Norwegian king who later became the patron saint of Norway.

Anne Skogsfjord, an archaeologist with the University of Oslo’s Museum of Cultural History, was the one who discovered the coin. She didn’t realize its significance at first, until she took a closer look at the inscription: “ONLAF R+ NORMANORV,” which means “Olaf, King of the Norwegians,” according to a statement.

She was shocked, as only four coins of that type had ever been found before, just one of which was discovered in Norway, during the restoration of church ruins in 1924. Fewer than 20 coins minted under Olaf have ever been found, and most have been discovered outside of Norway.
“I realized that we had found a national treasure,” she says in the statement.

Jon Anders Risvaag, a numismatist at the Norwegian University of Science and Technology, agrees with that characterization, adding that finding an Olaf coin is like “finding a needle in a haystack,” he tells Science Norway’s Ida Irene Bergstrøm. “There are so few of them.”

The obverse side of the coin features Olaf’s left-facing bust wearing a conical battle helmet, as well as a so-called Golgotha cross on three steps, inspired by Byzantine coinage. The other side depicts a double cross and an inscription that means “My leader, my lord.”
The design, researchers say, is emblematic of Olaf’s bid to establish Christianity in Norway.

“It is a Christianization coin on a grand scale,” Svein Gullbekk, a numismatist at the University of Oslo, says in the statement. “We can see how Olaf used coinage to legitimize the new faith and to establish himself as a Christian king of European standing. This is branding.”

Only three types of coins were issued under Olaf’s reign, so the king and his inner circle were probably intimately involved in the design and production process. “We can almost imagine Olaf himself holding this coin in his hand,” adds Gullbekk.
Coin production in Norway didn’t really take off until Harald Hardrada came to power in 1045 C.E. For Olaf, minting coins was likely more of a political power move than anything else.
“It’s someone pulling out all the stops and showing that he can do what people do abroad,” Risvaag tells Science Norway. “It’s a demonstration of kingship.”

However, this particular coin may also have been used as currency. It bears numerous small cuts that appear to have been made by a knife, which was a method of testing the silver content during transactions.

Researchers think the coin was probably produced around 1024 to 1028, near the end of the Viking Age, then buried with the rest of the Mørstad hoard in the late 1040s. During those intervening years, the cut marks suggest it changed hands several times.

Olaf, born around 995, first discovered Christianity as a young man, when he joined Viking raids against England and France. He was baptized in Rouen, France, around 1013. He became king not long after and ruled from 1015 to 1028.

During his reign, he pushed for the acceptance of Christianity, and his 1024 religious code is considered the founding of the Church of Norway. His aggressive efforts to Christianize Norway sparked resistance, particularly in Trøndelag and the inland districts of eastern Norway, according to the museum.
Olaf was killed in 1030 and canonized in 1031. His popularity skyrocketed after his death, with churches and shrines built in his honor across the world.
- When Danish King Cnut conquered Norway in 1028, Olaf took refuge with his brother-in-law, Yaroslav the Wise, the Grand Prince of Kyivan Rus.
- Olaf’s comeback attempt in 1030 failed, resulting in his death at the Battle of Stiklestad.

Historical accounts of Olaf are relatively scarce, so the newfound coin offers a rare and valuable glimpse into his life and royal power. The museum plans to feature it in an upcoming exhibition on the Mørstad hoard, marking the first time any part of the cache will go on public display.
In the meantime, researchers are continuing to catalog the hoard—a process that’s not likely to wrap up any time soon. The cache now contains an estimated 5,500 coins, according to the latest count.
“I am beginning to think that the hoard may soon exceed 6,000 coins,” Florent Audy, who is overseeing the Mørstad hoard cataloging process, says in the statement.

articles.title: These Big, Fierce Birds Found Love in Australia—and Laid the First Southern Cassowary Eggs at the Adelaide Zoo in 34 Years

paras.en: Finding love isn’t always easy—especially if you’re a southern cassowary, a massive, solitary bird with an aggressive reputation. But conservationists in Australia seem to have cracked the matchmaking code: A female cassowary recently laid two eggs after being paired with a potential mate.

The large, bright green orbs are the first southern cassowary eggs laid at Adelaide Zoo in South Australia in more than three decades—and their arrival is an encouraging bright spot for a species facing an uncertain future.

“This is really exciting news for us because it has been 34 years since we’ve had successful cassowary chicks here at Adelaide Zoo, so the team and myself included are very excited,” says Erin Kasteliz, team supervisor for birds at the zoo, in a statement.

Native to Australia, southern cassowaries are huge flightless birds found primarily in Queensland’s Wet Tropics and Cape York Peninsula; they also live in New Guinea and eastern Indonesia. Weighing up to 175 pounds and standing more than five feet tall, they’re the third-largest birds in the world, trailing behind emus and ostriches.

Beyond their imposing size, southern cassowaries are known for their striking appearance. Inky-black feathers cover most of their bodies, contrasting with vibrant blue necks, two dangling red wattles and a Mohawk-like casque—a raised, bony structure—atop their heads.

Scientists don't know why cassowaries have casques atop their heads. But they recently discovered that this helmet-like head ornament fluoresces under ultraviolet (UV) light, a discovery that only deepens the mystery.

Southern cassowaries have been recorded eating more than 200 different kinds of plants, and they play an important role in maintaining rainforest diversity by dispersing seeds via their droppings. They’re mostly solitary creatures, but they aren’t afraid to use their powerful legs and sharp claws to defend their turf when necessary.

The International Union for Conservation of Nature considers southern cassowaries a species of least concern, but Australia lists them as endangered, with an estimated 4,400 individuals remaining on the continent. Their survival has been threatened primarily by habitat loss and fragmentation resulting from forest clearing for agriculture and infrastructure, but the species is also vulnerable to vehicle strikes, poaching, dog attacks and competition with feral pigs.

Some Australian zoos have captive populations, which are part of a breeding program managed by the Zoo Aquarium Association Australasia (ZAA). The organization maintains a studbook to help determine which birds should breed, with an overarching goal of maintaining genetic diversity.

Earlier this year, staff at the Adelaide Zoo got the go-ahead to try breeding their resident southern cassowaries: 10-year-old Martina and 13-year-old Jeffrey. Though the two birds seemed like a good match on paper, there was no guarantee sparks would fly when they met in person.

Chad Crittle, the zoo’s director, compared the team’s matchmaking efforts to online dating, where it “might look like everything lines up really well. We like the same things and you might like the same food, but when you actually meet, it doesn’t always work,” he tells the New York Times’ Jennifer Sinco Kelleher. “And the same can be for animals in a zoo setting as part of these programs.”

Fortunately, Martina and Jeffrey seemed to hit it off right away. When they were officially introduced in August, Jeffrey started preening Martina—and, later that same day, they copulated. After that, staff members saw them mating on "multiple occasions," Kasteliz says in the statement.

This month, caretakers were overjoyed when they spotted two, fluorescent green eggs in the birds’ enclosure. And, they say, more could be on the way, as cassowary clutches typically contain three to five eggs. Whenever Martina is done laying eggs, it will be Jeffrey’s job to incubate them.
According to Kasteliz, the eggs’ neon-green color helps them blend in with their surroundings.

“That color comes from pigment in the shell and helps camouflage the egg," she says in the statement. "In the wild, cassowaries live in dense rainforest and will find a safe area amongst the leaves to lay, so that green helps keep the eggs hidden from predators.”

Zoo staffers don’t know whether the eggs are viable and will ultimately hatch into chicks. However, the sheer fact that Martina laid the eggs is a major win, since breeding southern cassowaries in captivity is so tricky. If the eggs do end up being viable, the zoo expects to have chicks in about 50 days—and Jeffrey would be responsible for rearing them.

For now, the team is cautiously optimistic. They’re keeping an eye on Jeffrey and Martina, while also trying to give them their space. They plan to be largely hands-off to let Jeffrey “have his first go at doing this so he can learn,” Crittle tells the Times.

articles.title: Astronomers Detect the Oldest Known Fast Radio Burst, Spewed From an Ancient Galaxy Just Three Billion Years After the Big Bang

paras.en: About ten billion years ago, in a faraway galaxy, some astronomical object released a brief but extremely powerful burst of energy into the universe. Now, scientists have detected that flash and figured out where it came from.

The findings, published in the journal Science on October 8, mark the oldest fast radio burst (FRB) ever detected. The mysterious flash was produced during the early universe, so it can help scientists better understand the ancient cosmos.

“If you put this in human perspective, when the light left the source, the sun didn’t exist, the solar system didn’t exist, no humans existed,” says study co-author Manisha Caleb, an astrophysicist at the University of Sydney, to Jacinta Bowler at the Australian Broadcasting Corporation. “Civilization formed and we built radio telescopes, and then we just happened to look at the right patch of sky at the right time.”

The solar system formed about 4.6 billion years ago. A dense cloud of gas and dust collapsed and formed a swirling disk of material. It continued pulling in more space stuff until immense pressure in the core birthed the sun.

FRBs are short but powerful flashes of radio waves. The first one was discovered in 2007, and thousands of them have been detected ever since. However, scientists still aren’t sure what produces the outbursts. One possibility is that they originate from the merging of two neutron stars, extremely dense remnants of dead giant stars. Another hypothesis is that they’re emitted by magnetars, rare types of young neutron stars with powerful magnetic fields. Researchers previously showed that at least one FRB probably came from a magnetar, but that doesn’t mean all of them are made by these strange stellar leftovers.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Detecting and measuring FRBs, as well as the galaxies they came from, can help solve this puzzle, says study co-author Themiya Nanayakkara, an astrophysicist at the University of Sydney, to Scientific American’s Adam Kovac. The MeerKAT radio telescope array in South Africa detected the newly described flash of radio waves, dubbed FRB 20240304B, in March 2024. The different frequencies of energy within the burst—like the rainbow produced when white light passes through a prism—arrived at different times, suggesting that the FRB traveled through a lot of plasma in outer space before reaching Earth. (The greater the dispersion of frequencies, the longer the distance traveled.)
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Then, the researchers used NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) to pinpoint the FRB’s origins. Analyses revealed that it came from a primitive galaxy that formed roughly three billion years after the Big Bang, which happened 13.8 billion years ago.

“We thought it would be a big, nicely formed galaxy with lots of stars, and instead it was a little dwarf galaxy, although it was actively forming stars,” Caleb says in a statement. It also had a low amount of metal. That’s consistent with the idea that FRBs originate from magnetars, Nanayakkara and Caleb write for the Conversation, hinting that FRB 20240304B came from one.

While the findings don’t definitively solve the mystery of what exactly produces FRBs, they’re useful in other ways. Scientists can use the flashes to learn more about the distant universe, based on how they were affected by the material they passed through during their journeys to Earth.

“Our discovery is particularly important because we have shown that we can do this across approximately 80 percent of cosmic history,” Nanayakkara explains to Scientific American. “The further back we push FRB detections, the further we can map this otherwise unseen matter.”

Matthew Bailes, an astrophysicist at Swinburne University of Technology in Australia who wasn’t involved in the research, tells Donna Lu at the Guardian that the new study is “a validation of how powerful the FRBs are for probing the universe.”

The next step, according to the study authors, is to find more of them. They estimate that the MeerKAT telescope can detect several ancient FRBs each year, per the statement. The team has also secured time to use the JWST to identify the sources of other old FRBs.

“The more distant FRBs we find, the stronger the constraints we can place on the objects and emission mechanisms that produce them, the environments in which they occur and the distribution of matter across the universe,” Nanayakkara tells Scientific American.

articles.title: Apple CarPlay and Android Auto Make Your Phone Hot. Here’s How to Keep It Cool
articles.author: David Nield

paras.en: Android Auto and CarPlay have transformed the way people drive.

Rather than putting up with whatever infotainment systems car manufacturers have put together, we're now able to interact with our phones from our car dashboards—with our contacts, our music, our podcasts, and our mapping apps all available. And the list of supported vehicles just keeps growing.

Both the Google and Apple solutions for this are really simple to use too. Most of the time they'll connect up automatically once you've done the initial setup. What you might not realize, though, are the demands that Android Auto and CarPlay put on your phone. Your handset is essentially doing all the regular phone stuff and then powering a large tablet-like display at the same time. That typically includes constantly updating a map in real time.

With that in mind, your Android phone or iPhone can quickly start to lose battery life and heat up when it's connected to your vehicle, which you've perhaps already noticed. To keep your handset cool and your battery in good shape, here's what you need to do.
Go Wired if You Can (but Watch the Charging)

Wireless Android Auto and CarPlay are convenient, just like wireless charging is convenient, but it puts more stress on your phone. If you've got the option of a wired connection, that's preferable—but that introduces a new potential heat problem, which is that your phone will always be charging up.
To counter that, you can set charge limits (Battery and charging from Android Settings, Battery > Charging from iOS Settings), or simply make sure your phone is kept in a cool, dark spot of the car.

This wired option has the added bonus of letting you switch to airplane mode on your phone, which will go a long way to limiting heat. Again there's a trade-off though: No one will be able to reach you, and you'll need to have your maps, music, podcasts, and whatever else you need downloaded to your device in advance.

If you do stick with wireless Android Auto or CarPlay, try to avoid charging your phone at the same time, especially on the wireless pad built into the car’s dash (which generates more heat). You don't want to end up with a dead phone half way through the journey, so you may have to compromise at certain times.

As mentioned above, where your phone is in the car makes a real difference to how hot it's going to be. If you have your phone's interface up on your car dashboard, then you don't necessarily need to have it fixed to the dashboard, too, possibly under direct sunlight. The glove compartment will do just fine.

If you have a mount for your phone, think about attaching it in front of one of your car's air vents. Blasts of air conditioned air will significantly reduce how hot your handset gets, working like a DIY cooling system.

You might also want to think about taking the case off of your phone for the length of the trip, if your phone is fitted with one. Your handset is less likely to be dropped or knocked while you're driving anyway, and a case can trap the heat in.

The rules aren't too different to keeping your phone cool generally, though with the added wrinkle of needing to keep it connected to your car somehow. Make sure the cabin in general is at a comfortable temperature, though you're probably already doing that for your own sake. The bigger thing to remember is to avoid leaving your phone behind in a vehicle that's going to heat up in the sun if you're stopping off somewhere.

If your phone is hooked up to Android Auto or CarPlay, then it's probably got some work to do—whether it's getting you to a destination or streaming music. However, you can still reduce heat by keeping phone tasks down to a minimum. If your calls and (voice-activated) messages can wait, leave them until the end of the journey.

We mentioned offline syncing above, but it doesn't have to go along with airplane mode. If you sync your tunes, podcasts, and maps to your phone ahead of time, your handset has less work to do while you’re driving since it doesn’t need to pull data from the cloud while also constantly searching for a wireless signal as you travel. Less stress on the modem means less heat overall.

Both Apple Maps and Google Maps let you download maps ahead of a trip. In Apple Maps, tap your profile picture, then Offline Maps, then Add Offline Map and find your location. With Google Maps, tap your profile picture, then choose Offline maps > Select your own map to choose the coverage.

There may be times when your phone has to be charging, wirelessly connected, making calls, in direct sunlight, and streaming music over a cellular connection, but try to keep these times to a minimum. Check regularly on how hot your phone is getting while connected to Android Auto or CarPlay, so you can take action if needed.

articles.title: Oil Spills Wreak Havoc on the Bottom of the Ocean, Even a Decade Later
articles.author: Bob Berwyn

paras.en: This story originally appeared on Inside Climate News and is part of the Climate Desk collaboration.
Across hundreds of miles of the northern Gulf of Mexico, a deepwater ecosystem collapsed after the massive 2011 Deepwater Horizon oil and gas spill, and recovery is uncertain, new research concludes.

The study, published Monday in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, found that animal populations—including octopus, krill, squid, and shrimp—declined by 60 to 85 percent in the three and a half years after the spill, with few signs of recovery since. Krill and lanternfish, both foundational species in the Gulf’s food web, were among the hardest hit. The findings also suggest that the die-off is causing genetic bottlenecks that could further hinder ecosystem recovery.

The researchers identified it as the “fastest and most severe faunal decline reported for Earth’s largest ecosystem type” ever documented. The widespread die-off of marine organisms may also reduce the ocean’s ability to transport carbon dioxide from the atmosphere to the deep sea. After ruling out other factors, such as water temperature and oxygen levels, the researchers identified the Deepwater Horizon blowout as “the most parsimonious explanation” for the ecosystem’s collapse.

Comprehensive natural resource damage assessments and restoration efforts involving federal, state, and tribal trustees are ongoing. In 2016, BP agreed to a $20.8 billion settlement, including up to $8.8 billion for environmental restoration.

Remote ocean depths and habitats miles below the surface may seem buffered from the impacts of human activity, the authors wrote, but their findings suggest an industrial disaster pushed part of it into a diminished state with “limited resilience to facilitate recovery.” They said their findings also show that proposed industrial deep-sea mining could damage the ecosystem before baseline conditions are assessed.

A transoceanic drilling rig, operating for BP about 50 miles southeast of the Mississippi Delta, exploded on April 20, 2010. The explosion and fire killed 11 people and triggered the largest accidental marine oil spill in history.

Oil and gas spewed uncontrollably from the broken well nearly a mile deep for 87 days, ejecting 4.9 million barrels of oil at a rate of about 400 tanker trucks per day, enough to fill up 1.2 million cars. The spill also released about 7.7 billion cubic feet of fossil gas into the deep sea at a rate of 88 million cubic feet per day, enough to supply about 820,000 US homes. State and federal agencies, including the Environmental Protection Agency, also authorized BP to apply 1.84 million gallons of chemical dispersants to try to reduce the impacts.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Some of the oil and gas dissipated and was transported out of the deep Gulf of Mexico region. Some coated barrier islands and devastated coastal wetlands and shellfish habitat, and some settled onto the ocean floor, where currents can stir it back into the water. But enough hydrocarbon and chemical-dispersant remnants stayed suspended long enough to do almost immeasurable harm.

A series of studies since the spill have shown a wide range of toxic effects on marine organisms, from impaired development and reproduction to increased mortality and lasting health problems in dolphins and whales. The new paper suggests that lingering pollutants may interfere with some species’ ability to find mates in the dark by disrupting their highly developed sense of smell.

The impacts continue to ripple through the ecosystem, said lead author Tracey Sutton, a professor of marine and environmental sciences at Nova Southeastern University in Florida. A 2024 study found an 80 percent decline in deep-diving toothed whales, he said.

“We used to have a big resident population of sperm whales right off the Mississippi River, but we haven’t seen a sperm whale in 10 years,” he said. Large predators need big, occasional dense patches of prey, and those have disappeared, he added.

Scientists have developed accurate ways to count fish. For this study, they started with a baseline from nine months of sampling in 2011 and compared it with nine subsequent surveys between 2015 and 2023. The researchers sampled deep-pelagic habitat along a large grid around the spill site from about 650 feet below the surface to about a mile down. The deep-pelagic zone accounts for about 90 percent of the Gulf’s total volume.

Across a grid of stations, scientists on slippery decks lowered and hoisted nets that open and close at different depths, with experts from different species groups to identify the catch. They sampled around noon and midnight to account for species that migrate vertically each day. Ship-mounted scientific echosounders provided an independent check, measuring sound reflected by marine life in the water column.

The research is “comprehensive and carefully composed,” marine biologist Bruce Robison, a senior scientist at the Monterey Bay Aquarium Research Institute, said via email. “There is no other study that I know of with such an incredible number of net samples,” added Robison, who did not participate in the new study.
The research focuses on species that are not commercially fished and shows for the first time that human impacts can deplete marine life even in very deep ocean water, he said.

“It is important for the public to understand just how disastrous this oil spill was,” Robison said. “The Gulf has not recovered, and it’s been over 15 years.” Robison said other activities, such as deep-sea mining, could also have severe negative consequences for deepwater pelagic ecosystems by discharging wastewater containing metals or lubricants.

Three lines of evidence—net hauls, acoustic surveys, and genetic sampling—corroborate each other, which is “unusually strong evidence to support his conclusions,” said Jeffrey Drazen, a marine ecologist at the University of Hawaii at Manoa, who did not participate in the new study.
The study examines all possible causes of the decline and shows only one aligns with the scientific evidence, he said.
“Through logical elimination,” he said, “and without actually pointing a finger, they leave no doubt that the oil spill is the cause of the decline.”

articles.title: The MacBook Pro Max Just Dropped to Its Lowest Price Ever
articles.author: Luke Larsen

paras.en: An exciting new MacBook is rumored to be announced in just one week. If the reports end up being true, it'll be the most significant change to the lineup in many years, introducing a touchscreen OLED MacBook Pro. As exciting as it sounds, however, it's also the perfect opportunity to buy up the previous generation's M5 Max MacBook Pro at its lowest price ever.

That's especially significant considering the entire lineup got a price increase back in June. Right now, the 16-inch M5 Max MacBook Pro with 36 GB of RAM and 2 TB of storage is $3,499, which is 20 percent off the retail price and $400 cheaper than it was just a few days ago. And historically, this is $150 cheaper than this configuration has ever sold for.

This absolutely stacked version of the MacBook Pro is one of the most powerful laptops you can buy. The M5 Max is a huge upgrade over both the M4 Max and the M5 Pro, offering GPU performance we've never seen on a MacBook before. For content creators, media professionals, engineers, and AI enthusiasts, this is nearly as good as it gets. It can even play AAA games smoother than any Mac (outside of the new Mac Studio). In my testing, Cyberpunk 2077 could average over 60 frame per second on the Ultra preset without relying on upscaling.

paras.en: If you really want to get serious about AI performance, you'll want to upgrade to the 64-GB or 128-GB configurations—though third-party retailers like Amazon don't sell them. You'll have to buy directly from Apple for that, and the prices are exorbitant. But the 36-GB model that's on sale has plenty of juice for dipping your toe in the world of on-device AI, and it's a home run for video editors, designers, musicians, and engineers.

Beyond performance, it goes without saying that all MacBook Pros have the best speakers, displays, build quality, trackpads, and keyboards of just about any laptop. I test dozens of new laptops every year, and while some have come close (such as the Surface Laptop Ultra I just finished testing), none have taken the crown.

You might be wondering if waiting to see these new MacBooks next week is worth it. Maybe. I can't guarantee that this deal will stick around, and I don't know what these new MacBooks will be like. Rumors say that they will sport the same chip options as the current MacBook Pros, meaning we'd get an M5 Pro and M5 Max once again. So if you're mostly interested in the performance, you can save some serious cash by snagging this M5 Max deal.

articles.title: U.S. Marine indicted on charges in killing of Okinawan woman

paras.en: Oct. 25 (UPI) -- A 20-year-old U.S. Marine has been charged in the killing and robbing of a Japanese woman at a hotel in Okinawa.

Lance Cpl. Devin Jacob Ballard was indicted Sunday on a charge of robbery causing death in the killing of 39-year-old Anna Yagi, according to a copy of the indictment provided by the Naha Public Prosectors Office.

Prosecutors allege Ballard wrapped a telephone handset cord around Yagi's neck early on Oct. 3 "with intent to kill." They said he killed her and stole her backpack, which contained a wallet and other items.
Ballard, who has denied the allegations, was arrested the next day, the Okinawa Prefectural Police said.
He faces the death penalty or life in prison, if convicted.
III Marine Expeditionary Force is continuing to cooperate with the investigation, spokesman 1st Lt. Tyle Thomas said.
"We recognize the seriousness of the charges and will continue to cooperate fully with Japanese authorities in their ongoing investigation as the legal process moves forward," he said.

The arrest of Billard has increased scrutiny of the conduct of U.S. military personnel on Okinawa. Gov. Gent Koja and the prefecture's assembly have demanded a review of the pact that governs U.S. military-connected personnel in Japan.
III MEF commander Lt. Gen. Benjamin Watson imposed a 30-day midnight-to-5 a.m. curfew for U.S. troops on Okinawa through Nov. 8.

articles.title: Appellate court panel grills DOJ lawyers on Calif. voter fraud suit

paras.en: Oct. 25 (UPI) -- A federal appeals court panel, meeting in a rare Sunday session, appeared skeptical of arguments by the Trump administration as it pressed its demand for the state of California to set aside 20,000 ballots it claims could be cast by non-citizens.

The 9th Circuit Court of Appeals, based in San Francisco, convened on a videoconference two days after the Trump administration urged it to intervene in their lawsuit demanding that California election officials access a password-protected flash drive they say has the names of thousands of possible non-citizens believed to be on the state's voter registration list.
U.S. District Judge David Carter had already scheduled an emergency hearing on the matter for Tuesday but the Department of Justice sought and received an appellate court intervention on Sunday.

U.S. Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter last week gave the Los Angeles County Clerk and California Secretary of State two days to confirm they were reviewing the thousands of submitted names and were segregating possible ballots, which may have been cast by individuals listed on the thumb drive.

California officials called the request legally baseless and a last-ditch effort by the White House to intervene in next week's midterm elections, even after losing more than two dozen court challenges over the past year to force states to release their voter rolls.
During Sunday's hearing, the appellate judges appeared similarly skeptical, peppering the DOJ lawyers with pointed questions.

After government attorney Matthew Donnelly said the Trump administration came up with the names after carrying out a "rigorous process" using its own citizenship data, Judge Mark Bennett questioned whether state election workers could legally disqualify voters without "extraordinary proof" by the federal government.

"Congress and the California Legislature have said non-citizens can't vote. This lawsuit is about, 'We don't like the way you're sorting citizens from non-citizens,'" Bennett stated. "I just don't see [federal law] telling California how to do the sorting."

Judge Gabriel Sanchez, an appointee of President Joe Biden, also expressed significant skepticism about the legality of the remedies being sought by the Trump administration so close to election day and whether appellate court intervention is appropriate at this point.
California's attorney Samuel Siegel said the White House lacks the constitutional authority to tell California how to sort its ballots.

"If the federal government, if the Executive Branch wants that authority in the first instance, they need to go ask Congress for it, they haven't done that," Siegel said. "They ask this court to short circuit the democratic process and issue an order, not just on the eve of an election, but as an election is underway."

articles.title: Serbia's strongman leader Vucic concedes defeat to student movement

paras.en: Oct. 26 (UPI) -- Serbia's longtime nationalist leader Aleksandar Vucic conceded defeat Sunday in snap parliamentary elections to a student-led opposition movement.
"It is clear that we have lost these elections," Vucic told supporters at the headquarters of his Serbian Progressive Party as the results came in, according to a statement from his party.

"We don't have the final results. Many will be surprised, and you will realize how much some people have lied and what they have fabricated. I want to inform you that the student-led protest list has won."
The defeat of Vucic, who resigned as president Sept. 27 to seek a return to the prime minister's office, which he held from 2014 to 2017, followed two years of student-led protests.

According to projections by the independent election-monitoring organization Center for Free Elections and Democracy, the Student List was expected to win 140 seats in the 250-seat parliament and Vucic's SNS won 103 seats, with a handful of minority parties winning the remaining seven seats, Serbian news agency FoNet reported.
Radomir Saicic, an academic and a Student List candidate, celebrated the results Sunday night at the movement's headquarters in New Belgrade.
"This is a victory of courage over fear, a victory of hope over indifference, a victory of faith that Serbia can and must be different," he said, Beta news agency reported.

"Thank you for every step, every hour, every sacrifice and every moment in which you chose not to give up. Thank you to everyone who raised their voice, who stood together and who showed that the future of this country does not belong to a select few, but to all its citizens."

The snap election was called on Sept. 9, when Vucic dissolved parliament amid nearly two years of anti-government protests by students initially angry over the deaths of 16 people in the Nov. 1, 2024, collapse of a concrete canopy at Novi Sad railway station, viewing the incident as the product of government corruption and negligence.
The election results could have significant implications for the Balkan nation.

Under Vucic's rule, the country maintained close relations with Russia. Russian President Vladimir Putin had publicly expressed support for Vucic's run for the premiership. While the Student List campaigned on Serbia maintaining its stance against imposing sanctions against Russia, it also expressed support Ukraine's territorial integrity.

The victory could also signal closer ties with the European Union, although the Student List has pledged to maintain Serbia's traditional relations with Russia. Serbia has been a candidate for EU membership since 2012, but negotiations have largely stalled since 2021 under Vucic's leadership.

"Today, the people of Serbia turned out in record numbers to shape their country's future. Congratulations to the Student List on its victory in the parliamentary elections," EU Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said in a statement.

"We stand ready to support reforms on the rule of law, media freedom, the fight against corruption and strong democratic institutions, and to work together to advance Serbia's future in the European Union."
Marta Kos, EU commissioner for enlargement, said the election means "a new chapter can begin for Serbia."

"After nearly two years of protests for democracy, the rule of law and the fight against corruption, Serbians turned out in historic numbers," she said online, saying, "These are the very values at the heart of the European Union."
"The door to the EU is open, and we are ready to move forward together."

articles.title: Calypso Rose Receives Standing Ovation at 2026 Caribbean Music Awards: 6 Best Moments
articles.author: Kyle-Brandon Denis

paras.en: From the continued domination of Full Blown’s “Big Links” riddim and Kes’ globe-trotting touring success to major moments like Destin Conrad’s Roadrunner reggae-dancehall LP and Keznamdi’s triumphant Grammy win, it’s been quite the year for Caribbean music and culture. To celebrate, the scene’s brightest and buzziest stars descended upon the National Academy for the Performing Arts (NAPA) in Port of Spain, Trinidad, for the fourth annual Caribbean Music Awards (Sept. 18). The official broadcast premiered on the official Caribbean Music Awards YouTube page on Oct. 25.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Co-hosted by soca princess Nailah Blackman and Majah Hype, the “King of Caribbean Comedy,” the ceremony featured special performances from 1T1, Theomaa, FreeTown Collective, Mela Caribe, Christo, Lil Kerry, V’ghn, 450, Jah Mason, Harmonik, Muddy and more. With the addition of several new categories honoring fast-rising genres like Dennery segment, jab and bouyon, this year’s Caribbean Music Awards truly captured the breadth of the region’s sounds and styles.

Taking place in its namesake region for the first time this year, Trinidad & Tobago dominated the ceremony, with zess superstar Lady Lava taking home trophies and dancehall artist Prince Swanny beating out an all-Jamaican lineup to secure the dancehall album of the year award for his Saint LP. Several other Trinbagonian stars took home some hardware, including Kes and Ravi B.

Billboard’s Kyle Denis hosted a red carpet livestream on the ground in Trinidad, catching up with a bevy of stars, including Ayetian, Jessie Woo and Moliy. Inside NAPA, attendees were treated to a gorgeous stage that featured performances from legends like Haitian konpa superstar Alan Cavé and younger acts like 450 and Mela Caribe. Blackman opened the show with an ethereal, tightly choreographed staging of her new single “Lova Gyal,” while FreeTown Collective held it down for live music with their instrument-driven set.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Several Caribbean music giants were honored for their impact and influence. Billboard Hot 100-charting reggae and dancehall powerhouse Patra scored the Lifetime Achievement Award; global music icon Calypso Rose received the Elite Calypso Award; Cavé earned the Elite Konpa Award; and hip-hop giant Shyne took home the Global Ambassador Award.
Here are the six best moments from the 2026 Caribbean Music Awards.

- Yung Bredda Brings ‘Greatest Bend Over’ Full Circle Yung Bredda’s “Greatest Bend Over” was easily the biggest song on Full Blown’s incredibly successful “Big Links” riddim last year, so it was a shame that he was unable to join the brother duo (and Machel Montano and Ayetian) for their crowd-rocking “Big Links” medley at last year’s ceremony. When Majah Hype announced “Greatest Bend Over” as this year’s winner of soca song of the year, Bredda accepted the award in person alongside Full Blown — and in his home country, for that matter. Not only is the song still fresh, but this full-circle moment also made the whole riddim even sweeter. “First things first, I want to say ‘Thank you’ to the Most High God; you know I always put God first in everything,” he began his acceptance speech. “Thank you for such a wonderful team that I have behind me… we coming from since COVID time ’til now, and [we have] an even further journey to go. I want to thank each and every person out there that’s been supporting what we’re doing and all my music.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: - MOLIY Hits Her Signature ‘Shake It to the Max’ Dance While Accepting Award “Shake It to the Max” may have ultimately been deemed ineligible to compete for the 2026 Grammys, but MOLIY still got her awards moment for her career-skyrocketing dancehall crossover smash. Alongside collaborators Shenseea, Skillibeng, Silent Addy and Disco Neil, MOLIY beat out an incredibly stacked lineup that included Skippa (“WYFL”), Armanii (“BBB – Snapchat”), Jada Kingdom (“G.A.D.”), Vybz Kartel (“God Is the Greatest”), Valiant (“Passenger Princess”), Masicka (“Rich Sex”) and Ayetian & Govana (“Wah Yo Deh Pan”). MOLIY also won dancehall collaboration of the year for “Shake It to the Max.” Once Yung Bredda announced “Shake It to the Max” as the winner, MOLIY hit her signature waist-whining, hands-covering-face dance move before making her way to the stage. “When I wrote this song, I had no idea the doors it would open for me,” she said, her face beaming with pride and excitement. “I had no idea I would be welcomed into this amazing community. And I feel like I belong here! I feel like I might stay a while; I feel like y’all should get used to having me around!”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: - Alison Hinds Pops Out to Honor Patra Last year, Bajan soca superstar Alison Hinds made an appearance and gave a sweet shoutout to fellow Bajan musician Rihanna to celebrate 20 years of her classic debut single, “Pon De Replay.” This year, Hinds honored another fellow powerhouse woman when she presented Patra with the Lifetime Achievement Award. Patra, a Jamaican reggae star who frequently charted on the Billboard Hot 100 in the mid-’90s and recently starred in the buzzy British television series Get Millie Back, joins previous Lifetime Achievement honorees, including Marcia Griffiths, Machel Montano and Bounty Killer. Fittingly, Patra also closed out the ceremony with a career-spanning medley of hits. “I’ve gone through a lot, but I’m happy now,” Patra said during her tearful acceptance speech. “And, to my fans, you guys have been holding me down for years… I highly recommend to you ladies: Please love yourselves. And take care of yourself. Don’t be afraid to be alone and reassess stuff. Love who you are, okay? And stop going around talking about aging and being ungrateful. Be thankful!”

paras.en: - Jah Mason Celebrates Legacy of ‘My Princess Gone’ Jah Mason’s “My Princess Gone” is arguably one of the most beloved reggae ballads of the 21st century, and Mason proved as much when he took the stage to perform the classic at the 2026 Caribbean Music Awards. Taking the stage shortly after 450’s dancehall-driven set, Mason immediately spiked the crowd’s energy with the opening notes of “Princess,” and by the time the first chorus hit, the audience practically sang the song for him. Inside the NAPA, it was particularly difficult to loosen up the Caribbean Music Awards crowd, but Mason did so with little effort at all.

paras.en: - Grenada Takes Center Stage with V’ghn, Lil Kerry & Muddy From Spicemas to jab jab, Grenada has significantly upped its profile on the international stage this year. At the 2026 Caribbean Music Awards, three of the island nation’s most resonant voices — V’ghn, Lil Kerry and Muddy — mounted a high-energy medley of their three jab-hailing soca hits. V’ghn, who eventually won jab artist of the year and jab song of the year, kicked things off with a spirited rendition of his Terra D Governor-assisted “Jab Decisions.” That segment quickly gave way to Muddy’s “Payroll,” which snagged a coveted spot on Rolling Stone’s 100 Best Songs of 2025 list last year. As dancers filled the stage with the raw energy of the road, Lil Kerry closed out the medley with “Mayhem,” the anthem that earned him his second consecutive Grenada Road March title after winning with “Bury All” in 2025. Now, this is how you put on for your island and seize your moment in the spotlight.

paras.en: - Calypso Rose Receives Standing Ovation Calypso Rose easily had the best moment of the night — and it happened fairly early in the ceremony. Trinidadian soca artist Terri Lyons elegantly presented Calypso Rose with the Elite Calypso Honor in commemoration of her historic, boundary-obliterating career. Widely regarded as the “Mother of Calypso,” Rose was the first bonafide female calypso star in the Caribbean, and her incredible success and impactful lyricism even spurred the renaming of the Calypso King competition to Calypso Monarch instead. In 2019, Rose made her Coachella debut at 78 years old, marking the first time a calypso artist played a full set at the iconic festival and cementing her as the two-weekend extravaganza’s oldest performer to date. After a video package ran through Rose’s decades-long career, Lyons led the packed audience in a singalong of “Calypso Queen,” featuring animated ad-libs from the Queen of Calypso herself. It was truly heartwarming to watch multiple generations of artists and fans come together to honor a true pioneer while she’s still with us.

articles.title: Snubs & Surprises at 2026 Caribbean Music Awards: Is ‘Dansa’ Really a Dennery Segment Song?
articles.author: Kyle-Brandon Denis

paras.en: Lady Lava may have dominated the night with four wins, including female soca artist of the year and zess song of the year (“Bob the Builder”), but the fourth annual Caribbean Music Awards certainly avoided clean sweeps.

Co-hosted by Majah Hype and soca star Nailah Blackman at Trinidad & Tobago’s National Academy for the Performing Arts (NAPA) in Port of Spain on Sept. 18, this year’s Caribbean Music Awards marked the first time the ceremony took place in its namesake region. The official broadcast premiered on the official Caribbean Music Awards YouTube page on Oct. 25, delivering a star-studded celebration of the biggest and brightest stars across the contemporary Caribbean music scene.

This year, several new categories were added to the ceremony’s sprawling lineup, including much-needed spotlights of fast-rising genres like bouyon, jab and Dennery segment. Billboard’s Kyle Denis hosted a red carpet livestream on the ground in Trinidad, catching up with a bevy of stars, including eventual winners Kes and Ayetian, as well as the night’s biggest victor, Lady Lava.

Outside of Lava, several other acts took home multiple trophies at this year’s ceremony. Trinidadian brother production duo Full Blown took home three awards, including soca song of the year for “The Greatest Bend Over” (with Yung Bredda) and soca video of the year for “Good Spirits.” They tied as this year’s second-most awarded act alongside pop-dancehall princess Shenseea and French-Haitian konpa singer Joé Dwèt Filé, who swept the konpa and French-Caribbean fields with his smash hit “4 Kampé.” Skillibeng, Kes, V’ghn, Lila Iké, Masicka, Moliy, Ayetian, Silent Addy, and Ravi B also snagged multiple awards.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: In addition to over 50 competitive awards, several Caribbean music legends were honored for their timeless contributions to the culture. Billboard Hot 100-charting reggae and dancehall queen Patra earned the Lifetime Achievement Award; Victoire de la Musique winner Calypso Rose received the Elite Calypso Award; konpa giant Alan Cavé scored the Elite Konpa Award; and Belizean-born, Brooklyn-bred hip-hop and political icon Shyne snagged the Global Ambassador Award.
While the ceremony certainly had its heartwarming moments, there were also quite a few head-scratchers. Here are six of the biggest snubs and surprises from the fan-voted 2026 Caribbean Music Awards.

- Surprise: ‘Dansa’ Wins Dennery Segment Song of the Year When Klassik Frescobar’s “Dansa” was announced as the winner of Dennery segment song of the year, Saint Lucian Twitter was almost instantly set ablaze. Dennery segment, an offshoot of soca combining elements of kuduro and zouk with Kwéyòl lyrics and dancehall-esque attitude, was developed in Saint Lucia’s Dennery District. It’s a fast-rising, distinctly Lucian sound that finally got a spotlight at the Caribbean Music Awards for the first time this year, so it was no surprise that a Jamaican-American (Frescobar) beating out an all-Lucian lineup of songs would ruffle some feathers. The other nominees in the category were: “Clap” (Blackboy), “Freak Out” (Hollywood HP & Ricky T), “Life of Party” (Pimp Juice), “Nuh Nuh” (Mighty & Mikado), “Pain Killer” (Umpa & Mikado), “The Car” (Dezral & Jardel) and “Toko Doak” (Natoxie & Deejay Asap). While Frescobar recorded “Dansa” over a beat helmed by Lucian Dennery segment producer DJ Kalli, the track is closer to late-2010s Dennery segment than the genre’s current sound — and it’s notably lacking the Kwéyòl lyrics that are a foundational element of the style. In a TikTok posted to his official account a week after the ceremony, Frescobar joked that he was “just as confused as you guys were,” and Umpa, who won Dennery segment artist of the year, recently told Billboard that “‘Dansa’ had the potential to win’ because of its crossover commercial success relative to the rest of the nominees. Ultimately, this should’ve gone to a Lucian Dennery segment artist — preferably “Nuh Nuh” by Mighty and Mikado.

paras.en: - Snub: Lil Kerry & Muddy Go Home Empty-Handed Lil Kerry and Muddy have been instrumental in raising the Grenadian soca scene’s profile over the past year. Kerry clinched this year’s Grenada Road March title with his pulsating “Mayhem,” while Muddy landed a spot on Rolling Stone’s Best Songs of 2025 with his equally electric “Payroll.” Both artists also brought their high-octane, road-ready energy to the Caribbean Music Awards stage in NAPA, and they both earned nominations in this year’s newly established categories of jab artist of the year and jab song of the year. Nonetheless, neither artist could take down V’ghn, whose Terra D Governor-assisted “Jab Decisions” — a notable departure from his usual groovy soca — swept the jab field. Surely, we could’ve spread the wealth for a genre with just two categories?

paras.en: - Surprise: Prince Swanny Wins Dancehall Album of the Year Dancehall is one of Jamaica’s biggest cultural exports, so it’s always a surprise when an artist from another island snags an award in the genre. Trinidad’s very own Prince Swanny won dancehall album of the year for his slinky, sultry Saint LP, beating out a stacked up line-up that included Masicka (Her Name Is Love), Popcaan (Nothing Without Love), 450 (Pieces of Me), Valiant (Prove Them Wrong), Armanii (The Impact), Vybz Kartel (Viking – 10th Anniversary Edition) and Ding Dong (From Ding Dong to World Ding).

This year, Moliy attempted to do the same with “Shake It to the Max” — which also features Shenseea, alongside Skillibeng, Silent Addy and Disco Neil — but Masicka thwarted her attempt at a clean sweep by taking home dancehall video of the year for his steamy “Rich Sex” visual.

Garlin earned nods for male soca artist of the year, soca song of the year (“Carry It”), and soca collaboration of the year (“Flatten,” with Voice). Admittedly, the soca field was especially competitive this year, but “Carry It” truly deserved recognition for its expert balance of deft, culture-rooted lyricism and downright galvanizing melody.

articles.title: Jack White Mourns Brother Eddie Gillis, Longtime Manager of Third Man Pressing
articles.author: Jessica Lynch

paras.en: Jack White is mourning the death of his older brother, Edward “Eddie” Gillis, who managed Third Man Records’ Detroit vinyl pressing plant.

White shared the news in an Instagram post on Saturday (Oct. 24), writing that Gillis had died that morning “after having fought a tough battle against cancer.” “The world lost a beautiful soul today,” White wrote. “Ed was such a caring, funny and generous person that everybody loved.”

Gillis ran Third Man Pressing for 10 years, overseeing the production of “hundreds of thousands” of records for other artists, White wrote, adding that his brother liked to make small sculptures and flowers from the plant’s vinyl scraps. The facility opened in 2017 in Detroit’s Cass Corridor as part of White’s Third Man Records operation, making White one of the few artists to own his own pressing plant. Before that, Gillis worked as a pastry chef, running kitchens and bake shops for the Ritz-Carlton and Beaumont Hospital.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: White, the youngest of 10 siblings, also credited Gillis with shaping his musical start. “In his youth Eddie was the guitar player in the family when we were all growing up back when I was on drums only, and he was just great at the instrument,” he wrote, recalling that the two played together over the years, once for the Detroit Tigers during spring training in Florida. “He taught me so many wonderful and simple things over the years that I’ll never forget; how to string a guitar, how to fish on the Detroit river, how to drive a stick shift,” White added. “He was an amazing big brother to me and I just hate to see him leave, but I’m glad he is at peace.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Gillis is survived by his wife, Angie, and their two children, Amelia and Garrett.

White rose to fame as one half of the White Stripes, whose “Seven Nation Army” topped Billboard’s Alternative Airplay chart. As a solo artist, he has sent three albums to No. 1 on the Billboard 200: Blunderbuss (2012), Lazaretto (2014) and Boarding House Reach (2018). Lazaretto also set the record for the biggest vinyl sales week since 1991, a mark it held until 2021.

articles.title: Eric Bauza, the Modern Voice of Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck and Other Iconic Characters, Dies at 46
articles.author: Kimberly Nordyke

paras.en: Eric Bauza, an Emmy-winning voice actor who was the modern voice of Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck and other Looney Tunes characters, has died. He was 46.

The news was announced Sunday by his family via a post on his Instagram feed. “Eric Bauza, Emmy Award-winning voice actor and the modern voice of iconic Looney Tunes characters Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, along with dozens of other beloved cartoon characters, has passed away suddenly. More details to come,” the post reads.

It’s unclear when he died, but he was scheduled to attend the premiere of Warner Bros. Pictures Animation’s The Cat in the Hat on Sunday afternoon to support Daffy Season, a short that plays before the film, according to press documents.
Channing Dungey, chairman of Warner Bros. Television Group and U.S. Networks, paid tribute to Bauza in a statement.

“Eric Bauza was a unique voice talent who brought joy and laughter to millions around the world. During his 15 years at Warner Bros. Animation,” she said. “He was the voice of Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck among countless other characters. He followed in the footsteps of giants like Mel Blanc. Eric said that carrying on the legendary legacy of the Looney Tunes was among the greatest honors of his life. In addition to his incredible talent, Eric was a treasured part of our animation family. Our hearts go out to his loved ones.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Bauza recently landed on The Hollywood Reporter’s inaugural Animation Power list and attended the corresponding event honoring those on the list. “Bauza has quietly become the voice of an entire cartoon universe,” THR’s Scott Roxborough wrote of the voice actor. “One of the successors to the legendary Mel Blanc as the voice of Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck, Marvin the Martian and a dozen more iconic characters, the Canadian actor outdid himself with Coyote vs. Acme, voicing everything from Bugs Bunny to Foghorn Leghorn and Tweety Bird.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: “A lot of talented folks worked really hard to make this film, and to be able to see it celebrated by so many people across the globe has really made the wait worth it,” Bauza said of the movie.

In the Looney Tunes film Coyote vs. Acme, which was released earlier this year, Bauza voiced several roles, including Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck, Tweety, Daffy Duck, Elmer Fudd, Foghorn Leghorn, Porky Pig, Road Runner, Charlie the Dog, and more. Most of those roles, of course, originated with the late, legendary Mel Blanc. Bauza also brought several Looney Tunes characters to life in such productions as Space Jam: A New Legacy (voicing Daffy Duck, Porky Pig, Foghorn Leghorn, Elmer Fudd and Marvin the Martian) and Looney Tunes Cartoons (Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck), among others.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Born December 7, 1979, Bauza was from Toronto but more recently was living in Los Angeles.
He started his career in animation as a character designer working with a few production studios in Hollywood, according to his bio on SBV Talent, which represented him.

He received Daytime Emmy, Children’s & Family Emmy and Annie Award nominations for his work as the title character in The Adventures of Puss in Boots, Fozzie in Muppet Babies and Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck in Looney Tunes Cartoons.
Recently, he voiced roles in DreamWorks Animation’s animated film Forgotten Island.

His other TV credits include Unikitty, Archibald’s Next Big Thing, The Rocketeer, Ballmastrz: 9009, Rise of the Teenage Mutant Turtles, Star vs. The Forces of Evil, Breadwinners, Uncle Grandpa, Atomic Puppet, The Powerpuff Girls, The Fairly OddParents, Ultimate Spider-Man, Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, Guardians of the Galaxy, Transformers: Robots in Disguise, Sanjay and Craig and Mighty Magiswords.
Bauza has voiced characters in The Book of Life and The SpongeBob Movie: Sponge Out of Water. Bauza also was Woody Woodpecker in Universal’s animated film Woody Woodpecker.

According to his bio, Bauza has also voiced characters in commercials, including Lucky the Leprechaun for Lucky Charms cereal, Trix Rabbit for Trix cereal and Marvin the Martian for Nike and in the Walmart commercial “Famous Visitors.”

articles.title: Donald Trump Attacks Bill Maher in Scathing, 1,318-Word Social Media Post: “Complete and Total Loser”
articles.author: Kimberly Nordyke

paras.en: President Donald Trump is once again criticizing Bill Maher, host of HBO‘s Real Time With Bill Maher — only days after the two had what he previously referred to as a “great dinner” at the White House.
On Sunday, Trump posted a scathing 1,318-word diatribe on Truth Social blasting Maher as a “complete and total loser” (in all caps).

“Let’s talk about this COMPLETE AND TOTAL LOSER, Bill Maher,” he began. “He’s got a Low Rated Show on equally Low Rated HBO, which was once, long ago, a Network of Quality and Excitement — But that’s all gone. It’s not ‘HOT’ anymore!” (Capitals and uppercasing are all Trump’s.)

Trump then turned his ire to producer Chuck LaBella, who’s worked with Maher for years across multiple productions, nothing that LaBella was a “gofer” on Trump’s reality competition show The Apprentice, and also a friend of Trump’s at the time.

“[B]ecause of the success of that show, Number One and Top Rated on many weeks, with the Finale’ [sic] being among the Top Shows of the Year, he was automatically and quickly brought up through the Ranks of NBC, along with everyone else associated with that Historic ‘Happening,'” Trump wrote. “The Success of the Apprentice was so great that everyone partook — It built many careers, and that is a wonderful thing. Some people say it even built my career, because I became President (I would have won without it!). In any event, over the last few years, LaBella would call me nonstop to say, ‘Hello,’ be very nice, and tell me how much Bill Maher ‘loves’ and respects me, and would constantly ask of me, even before I was President, for any form of meeting with Maher and, would I do his show? When I became President, I agreed to meet, after the first one, and the last one, but never agreed to do his show, which he wants me to do, DESPARATELY [sic] — It won’t happen! When I have watched the show, which isn’t often, it always ends with dishonesty, about me at least, but, who cares?”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Trump apparently was upset with Maher over some jokes made on Friday’s installment of Real Time. In his monologue, Maher mocked the president’s approval ratings and recent comments about men’s physiques, while referring to his own recent visit to the White House.

“It’s just a little odd that Trump keeps gushing about men’s bodies, and how handsome they are, and their jawlines, and their asses, their physiques,” Maher said. “I’m a little hurt. I was there for dinner for four hours last week, and not a peep. Nothing.”
He added: “Trump has the lowest approval rating of any midterm candidate ever. Only 1 percent of the Republicans are mentioning him in their ads.”
In his post, Trump cited several polls claiming Trump is the most popular Republican of all time, beating out both Ronald Reagan and Abraham Lincoln.

Also on the show, Maher made a joke about Ohio Republican gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy, who ran an ad featuring Democrat gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton’s mother, Donna Arthur, calling her daughter “a liar.” Actor and Arthur reportedly have not been in touch since 1978, when Arthur’s second husband, Cledith Arthur, was indicted and charged with raping Actor, who was 12 at the time. The Ramaswamy campaign has said it will spend $4 million to promote the ad Ohio, with Trump and Vice President JD Vance both backing the decision to run the spot.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: “Trump said this is fair game,” Maher said on his show. “A 12-year-old rape victim is fair game? I know that looks bad. It sounds better on a birthday card to Jeffrey Epstein.”

Trump and Maher had dinner at the White House earlier this month with Stephen A. Smith and Kid Rock. Afterward, Trump told reporters: “It was a great dinner. It was a very informative dinner, Smart people. Stephen A. is great. Bill Maher — I will tell you what. He likes me a lot more than people understand, and I actually like him. It was a good dinner.”

However, on Sunday, in his Trump Social post, Trump called Maher or LaBella a “pothead” and said he “looked like hell this time” (it’s really unclear which person he was referring to). He also said that Maher “was drunk and had alcohol in his hand as he walked through the White House.”
The president also wrote that Maher “lies about everything” and accused him of using a “Laughter Machine [sic]” because his jokes “aren’t funny or even any good.”
Trump then recalled their first dinner together, in March 2025, and how that came about.

“Chuck LaBella, and my friend, Kid Rock, called me incessantly about meeting with Bill Maher,” Trump wrote “My first response was, ‘Fellas, this guy’s a Goofball.’ They said, ‘He wants to go down to the White House, be with you, and talk. He said you’re very smart, but you’re not into the Liberal Platform. Will you start thinking about it?’ He invited himself to the White House! We had our first meeting, Bill was very nervous. He asked for a drink. He was very insecure, and he had a seriously bruised eye and nose area, as though somebody had just beaten him up — But it wasn’t me!”

paras.en: After that dinner, Trump was at first complimentary but then later criticized Maher. On Sunday, Trump claimed LaBella pushed hard for a second dinner. He also disputed Maher’s statement that the second dinner lasted four hours.

“Overall, I thought it was a good meeting,” he wrote. “It didn’t last four hours, it lasted two hours, maybe less, and everybody was happy. We have the timestamps. I learned nothing, and felt it was a waste of time. After the first dinner, Bill Maher was friendly, I guess, everyone walked away pleased. He gave me a good first show, with lots of Laughing Machine laughter, which is a real term, but it is what it is, and then reverted back to his former self, and his old ways. I understand that. He’s doing his thing. I never took it very personally. I would always mock his Low Ratings, whenever I heard. He’s not a nice guy, and what he spouts isn’t what he believes. He has to cater to his base, which is mostly composed of Losers, and people who don’t like working.”

If I hadn’t won the Election, it would be DEAD! Also, turn your Laugh Machine off, it’s a joke when they laugh uncontrollably, even when you say nothing funny, and I’m going to have the Republicans not cover you anymore, because they try to talk about you as a guy who is transformative. You’re not transformative, you’re a Loser! I never watched your show much, but I will never watch it again, because it is nothing more than FAKE NEWS that America, and the World, is unfortunately subjected to. Thank you for your attention to this matter. President DONALD J. TRUMP”
